questions.q: According to the summary, what are the four forms of love in the New Testament?
a: Erotic, brotherly, familial and unconditional
Romantic, practical, spiritual and lasting
Young, mature, familiar and divine
Passionate, patient, faithful and kind
questions.why: Lesson 1 traces love from passion through friendship and family to selfless love.

questions.q: Which form of love does the summary warn can become monotonous if it lasts too long?
a: Familial love
Erotic love
Brotherly love
Unconditional love
questions.why: Lesson 1 says staying too long in familial love can make a relationship dull.

questions.q: Why does the summary compare love languages to speaking different languages?
a: People show affection differently, so learn to recognize their gestures
Couples should always use exactly the same words
Most arguments come from poor grammar and wording
Only one love language can be learned at a time
questions.why: Lesson 2 says understanding your partner's signals helps you appreciate them.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest breaking relationship boredom?
a: Do something you both enjoy, like a short trip or date
Spend more evenings apart from each other
Rework your household budget together
Talk only about the children and schedules
questions.why: Lesson 2 names routine as a threat and recommends shared novelty.

questions.q: What attitude does the summary recommend during hard times in marriage?
a: Pray for chances to learn, listen and forgive
Wait quietly for your partner to change first
Focus on everything they are doing wrong
Avoid discussing problems with anyone else
questions.why: Lesson 3 says difficulties are opportunities and prayer builds patience and gratitude.
